A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CountLLM study, with readable text, equations, figures, and tables. All 11 pages were compared; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. Pages 2–11 have identical extracted text and rendered images.

before.justification: v1 reports original CountLLM benchmark evaluations, generalization experiments, and ablations in Tables 1–7, plus qualitative counting results in Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original CountLLM evaluations, generalization results, and ablations in Tables 1–7 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same four-component architecture, periodicity prompts, standardized answer format, handling of split action cycles, and three-stage training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use WebVid-10M for alignment training and retain RepCount, UCFRep, Countix, and OVR-Kinetics evaluations. Cross-dataset tests and the animal, cartoon, and non-living-motion scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding Tables 1–4 and Figure 5, including ESCounts in the benchmark comparisons, OVRCounter on OVR-Kinetics, and the same video MLLMs in the qualitative comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same validation/test usage, MAE and OBO metrics, encoder configurations, training epochs, and frame-sampling procedure. The cross-dataset evaluation design also remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 5–7 retain identical ablations of instruction components, alignment stages, the periodicity transformer, and LoRA adaptation. The cross-dataset and out-of-domain analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative outcomes in Tables 1–7 and Figure 5 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains CountLLM with VideoMAE at RepCount MAE 0.162 and OBO 0.639 in both versions.

T1.justification: The counting formulation, model equations, and training objectives in Equations 1–11 are identical, as are the metric definitions in Equations 12–13. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the first LLM-based RAC framework, structured periodicity instructions, progressive training, benchmark performance, and out-of-domain generalization.

C2.justification: The explanations involving periodicity awareness and reduced overfitting are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same qualifications about GPU requirements and possible improvements through more precise descriptions and in-context examples.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including Vicuna-7B, 64 periodicity queries, a 12-layer transformer, LoRA rank 16, and eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 66 references are unchanged. The positioning relative to regression-based counting methods and general-purpose video MLLMs is identical.

P1.justification: The first-page affiliation corrects 'University of Washingtong' to 'University of Washington', and the arXiv version/date stamp updates. The remaining prose, terminology, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All five figures and seven tables retain their formatting, captions, and placement. Pages 2–11 render identically, while the first page retains its layout with only affiliation and version/date text changes.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects an affiliation spelling error and updates the version/date stamp. This provides a negligible editorial benefit; the methods, evidence, scientific explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
